packageRules.description: Automatically merge GitHub Actions dependency updates after Renovate observes green CI.

agent-desktop is built by this repository's own pipeline. Its pin lives in devcontainer-compose-pins.yml, outside the CI image path filter, so merging a bump cannot retrigger the build that produced the digest and bump itself again. That is what makes automerge safe here.

The image's Ubuntu base release is not bumped by Renovate: it stays at 24.04 because downstream consumers depend on that release. Another Ubuntu release ships as a separately named image tag with an explicit base, never as a bump of this one.

pre-commit hook revisions, the renovate-config-validator hook's among them: its rev is the Renovate version the bot and the validation workflow run. A rev bump edits .pre-commit-config.yaml, which runs the required validation check at the new version before it can merge.

Super-Linter and the pre-commit/local tools it pins (Prettier, clang-format, Ansible Lint, Hadolint, Ruff, ShellCheck, Gitleaks, Actionlint, Zizmor) must stay in sync with the pinned Super-Linter image. Update them manually with the sync-super-linter-tool-versions skill instead.
Prettier's additional_dependencies pin in the mirrors-prettier hook is synced manually alongside the mirror revision; see the rule above.

The provisioning tools the Ansible roles pin, including the checksum-carrying downloads. The post-upgrade script recomputes every checksum in the same commit as the version and fails the branch when it cannot, so no bump leaves a role half-updated. That is what makes batching and automerge safe here.

uv is pinned twice: the setup-python-venv action input CI runs on, and the uv_setup role the image ships. Grouping them keeps both in one PR so CI never validates against a different uv than the image carries.

customManagers.description: The devcontainer CLI version the post-upgrade script regenerates the devcontainer lock with.
Versions of the checksum-carrying tools in dev_tools_pinned_tools: an entry's unquoted `version:` field, under a `# renovate:` comment that may name a versioning scheme for prefixed tags.
Version pins in the Ansible roles' defaults, each tagged by a `# renovate:` comment on the line above it.
Commit pins in the Ansible roles' defaults, for upstreams whose tags are unusable. The comment carries the branch the commit is tracked on.
